written.myAnswer: Sensitivity is a thermometer’s ability to detect small changes in temperature.
A thermometer is linear when equal temperature changes produce equal changes in the scale reading.
Use a larger bulb and a narrower capillary tube, so a small temperature change produces a greater movement of the liquid column.

Sensitivity is the ability to detect small temperature changes; range is the span between the lowest and highest temperatures a thermometer can measure; and linearity means equal temperature changes produce equal scale changes. For example, 0.1°C divisions indicate greater sensitivity than 1°C divisions; a clinical thermometer has a narrow range, commonly about 35°C to 42°C; and a linear thermometer has evenly spaced markings for equal temperature intervals.

Sensitivity can be increased with a larger bulb and a narrower capillary. Range can be extended by using a suitable thermometric liquid with a low freezing point and high boiling point, and a sufficiently long tube. Linearity is improved by using a liquid that expands uniformly and a capillary with a uniform bore.
